text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-Nearly 40 Norwegian highways are closed because of snow and danger of avalances. In Nordland, a northern county, 30 people were evacuated from their homes on Sunday because of bad weather. Two people were killed on Friday by an avalance near the Arctic town of Tromsoe.
-Over the last two years Norway has received considerable financial support from the European Union for research. Over 400 research jobs are now financed by EU means.
-The Norwegian Central Bank reacted too late, German macro experts say in commenting Norway's rate cuts last week.
-Cuts in interest rates increase demand for real estate. Prices rose by 10 percent in 1996 and experts expect prices to rise by the same percentage in 1997.
-Norway's Fokus Bank will cut costs by 80 million crowns per year. Year the share has risen by 12 percent to 49 crowns so far this year.
- Industrial group Aker and investment group RGI spent 100 million crowns on consultancy fees to brokerhouses as part of their merger last year.
